chunks: 90 - That which informed me was Abu Abdullah Ahmad ibn Abdun, known as Ibn al-Hashir, who said: Narrated to me Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Shuja'i the scribe, who said: Informed us Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, known as Ibn Abu Zainab al-Nu'mani the scribe, who said: Informed us Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Allan al-Dhahabi al-Baghdadi in Damascus, who said: Narrated to us Abu Bakr ibn Abu Khaithama, who said: Narrated to me Ali ibn al-Ja'd, who said: Narrated to me Zuhair ibn Mu'awiya from Ziyad ibn Khaithama from al-Aswad ibn Saeed al-Hamdani, who said: I heard Jabir ibn Samra say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say:

After me, there will be twelve Caliphs, all of them from Quraish. He said: When he returned to his house, Quraish came to him and said: Then what will happen? He replied: Then there will be confusion (al-Harj).
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say would happen after the twelve Caliphs from Quraish?
ai.summary: This hadith, cited by Shaykh al-Tusi in *Kitab al-Ghayba* to validate the number of Imams, is a cornerstone of Shia eschatology, linking the twelve Caliphs to the twelve Imams from the Prophet's progeny. The term 'al-Harj' signifies the era of political fragmentation and civil strife that followed the Rashidun period, marking the transition from the era of Caliphate to the era of Imamate. Its inclusion in Sunni sources underscores the widespread acceptance of the twelve-leader framework across Islamic traditions.
